label: Mirror link shape is per-kind and per-runtime, not per-kind: .cursor/agents/* resolves to ../../.claude/agents/* (11 links) while .claude/agents holds 13 copies and 0 symlinks, so deleting .claude/ dangles 11 Cursor agent links and a copy-based drift check comparing .claude/agents against .skilled/agents cannot see that .cursor follows .claude. .opencode/commands, by contrast, links to ../../.skilled/commands/*. The Claude copies are legitimately runtime-specific (tools: Read, Bash, Grep, Glob vs the source's opencode permission: block), so 'stale copy' is not the claim. Orphan: .claude/agents holds 13 files against 12 in .skilled/agents; Explore.md exists only in the mirror.

symlink-engine.cjs check returns 0 unconditionally after emit, so the install workflow's single read-only proof cannot fail: run against an empty /tmp target it printed 'missing core .skilled' (and 3 more, and 6 more with --link-instructions) and exited 0 in all three variants. No doctor caller gates on its exit code, and the three documents that invoke it already disagree on the flag surface (_routes.yaml:553 and doctor-symlink-check.yaml:57 vs doctor-install.yaml:59, which omits --include and --json). Nothing breaks today because every caller renders lines; the risk is that install.yaml's other steps do treat 'exit 0' as 'build exists', so the same idiom applied to check would read green over an empty target.

A fully healthy sk-git setup reads as STATUS=DEGRADED exit 3 on six of seven runtimes: the battery auto-detects only CLAUDECODE (active = explicit ? '--tool' : 'CLAUDECODE'), so from a Pi session nine rows PASS and ai-tool-hooks is UNKNOWN with all seven adapters listed as registered, yielding degraded=0 unknown=1 and exit 3. renderHuman prints repair: only for FAIL and DEGRADED, so the single row that caused exit 3 is the one row with no repair line. /doctor:setup compensates by passing --tool explicitly while /doctor:git setup only instructs the model to add it, so two routes to the same battery disagree on whether the flag is supplied or requested. Drifts against the v4.0.0.11 note's 'It works in all seven AI tools' and 'A half-working setup no longer reads as healthy'.

The v4.0.0.14 fsmonitor claim holds today (cite-drift-scan 5 git calls / 6 GIT_NO_FSMONITOR mentions, check-source-tags-helper 3 / 4, and validate.sh itself makes no git call) but the guard that keeps it true accepts a constant name rather than a value: FSMONITOR_OFF is /core\.fsmonitor=false|FSMONITOR|GIT_CONFIG_/ tested against the whole call text, so GIT_NO_FSMONITOR satisfies it even if redefined as []; the shell scanner in the same file instead requires the literal core.fsmonitor=false on the line, so the two scanners disagree on what 'off' means. Narrowing the alternation to FSMONITOR_OFF keeps all eight current call sites matching.

Three release claims tested and confirmed: v4.0.0.11's eleven checks (CHECKS array has exactly 11 entries), v4.0.0.12's 17 doctor commands (ls *.md = 17) and its advisor leg (advisor_status with --workspace-root $PWD returned exit 0, freshness live, skillCount 16, indexStaleness fresh), and v4.0.0.14's fsmonitor coverage.

Symlink census at HEAD: .claude 79/109, .codex 26/90, .cursor 81/92, .devin 41/61, .dsh 79/156, .opencode 23/4024, .pi 58/50112. Per kind: .claude/agents 13 entries 0 links; .codex/agents 11/0; .cursor/agents 11/11; .devin/agents 11/0; .dsh/agents 11/0; .pi/agents 11/0; .dsh/skills 55/55; .cursor/commands 46/45; .opencode/commands 10/9; .claude/commands 7/1; .codex/prompts 45/0; .pi/prompts 46/0; .dsh/prompts 45/0.

A mirror entry is either a link to the canonical source or a copy with runtime-native frontmatter; a link to another mirror is a third shape no manifest row names, and only .cursor/agents exhibits it.
A read-only check that always exits 0 is a reporter, not a gate; any caller that treats exit 0 as 'installed' inherits a green result over an empty target.
